newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish pensioners to get PLN 1.4 bln compensation.
newsitem.headline: Polish pensioners to get PLN 1.4 bln compensation.

text.p: The Polish government can earmark up to 1.4 billion zlotys next year to compensate pensioners for pay rises they should have been offered earlier this year, PAP news agency reported on Wednesday.
PAP quoted deputy labor minister Maciej Manicki as saying that this was the maximum sum that would not require increasing next year's budget deficit, planned at 2.8 percent of gross domestic product.

The payout for pensioners stems from a constitutional court ruling in July that pensions should have been increased in March, as was envisaged by the social security law which was effective until the end of 1995.

The law was changed as of January this year as a prelude to a planned social security reform and the new legislation offered pensioners a 2.5 percent real pay increase this year, to be made in September.

The Tribunal, which decides whether laws are compatible with the constitution, ruled that the pensions rise should have been granted in March because it was linked to wage growth in the last quarter of 1995, when the old law was still effective.
